justification: Changes Housing SEPP eligibility answers and the 'Housing SEPP (LMR): Applicable' badge for every residential lot: whether a lot is in a Low and Mid-Rise housing area now comes from the SEPP map layers (Town Centres 766, TOD 752/759, exclusions 776) via a new Python endpoint, replacing a hardcoded list of 47 council names that put 19 of 23 residential panel lots in a reform area they are not in.

falsifiable_check.command: python -m pytest tests/test_housing_sepp_gates_api.py -q && cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/api/housing-sepp-lmr-gate-states.test.ts __tests__/components/compliance/PathwaySummaryCard-lmr.test.tsx --ci
falsifiable_check.fails_when: Mutation measured 2026-10-18: eligibility route treating an unknown area as inside (isLMRArea !== false) -> 4 failed / 10 passed across the two route tests; restored -> pass. Python tests assert None propagates (a layer that does not answer never yields False).
falsifiable_check.observed_red: The mutation above; first full jest run failed 1 (PathwaySummaryCard test matched another line's 'Not applicable') until scoped.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: NSW Planning Portal SEPP layers 766/752/759/776/452 queried live. Parity: the new endpoint agrees with services/housing_sepp_eligibility._gate_inputs on all 28 rules-per-address panel addresses (28 agree, 0 differ, 0 unknown), 2026-10-18; live check 6 Berrigan St Winston Hills in_lmr_area False, near_town_centre False.

pre_impl.existing_data: services/housing_sepp_eligibility._gate_inputs already derived the area from the map layers for the Site Report; lib/regulatory-constants.ts STAGE2_REGION_LGAS (47 councils) decided it on the website; the code itself flags the TS route as an independent reimplementation (DQ-30).
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: Assumed the two engines agreed on reform areas because both cite the same SEPP; measured: the website said in-area for every residential panel lot, the map says 4 of 23.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: One small Python module reusing the existing portal_constraints fetchers, one Next proxy route and one hook; the TS eligibility route keeps its other logic (full consolidation into Python is a separate follow-up).
pre_impl.external_source_error: Each layer is reported true/false/null; a failed or slow layer makes in_lmr_area null, the badge reads 'Not checked: the planning map did not answer' and LMR forms are 'not assessed', never 'not applicable' or eligible.
pre_impl.frontend_type: gates {in_lmr_area, in_tod, near_town_centre, town_centre, lmr_excluded, dual_occ_prohibited} each boolean|null; card and route isLMRArea boolean|null; PathwaySummaryCard housingLmrApplicable boolean|null.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Worst case a lot inside a reform area shown as outside it (false negative) if the map is wrong; the layers are the Planning Portal's own SEPP maps, so this follows the source.

functions.name: lmr_gates
functions.input: latitude and longitude of the lot, queried against the SEPP map layers
functions.output: true, false or null for each gate and the combined Low and Mid-Rise area answer
functions.if_none: in_lmr_area is null whenever the answer depends on a layer that did not answer

functions.name: POST /api/housing-sepp/eligibility
functions.input: zone, lot size, width range and isLMRArea true, false or null from the map gates
functions.output: per-form result: LMR forms ineligible outside an area, not assessed when unknown, unchanged inside
functions.if_none: an absent or null isLMRArea gives 'not assessed: could not be checked', never eligible

values.value: no new numbers; area rule and distances come from the existing portal_constraints fetchers

values.read_at: lmr_gates vs _gate_inputs on run8 panel coordinates, 2026-10-18
values.if_missing: without it the two engines could still disagree

break_it.scenario: Lot far from any town centre or station in a Greater Sydney council (Winston Hills).
break_it.what_happens: Badge reads 'Not in a Low and Mid-Rise housing area' and multi-dwelling is not eligible.
break_it.how: Map gates instead of council list; live integration test.

break_it.scenario: Planning Portal town-centre layer times out for the lot.
break_it.what_happens: Area is null; badge reads 'Not checked'; LMR forms are not assessed, not passed or failed.
break_it.how: None propagation in lmr_gates; route treats null as unknown; tests.

break_it.scenario: A caller still sends no isLMRArea at all (AI assistant router).
break_it.what_happens: Forms that require the area are 'not assessed', never treated as inside the area.
break_it.how: Route reads only isLMRArea === true as inside; mutation to !== false goes red.

break_it.scenario: Lot inside the exclusion map but next to a town centre.
break_it.what_happens: Area is false: excluded land is outside the reform area whatever its anchor says.
break_it.how: excluded True forces False in lmr_gates; Python test case.

break_it.scenario: Python service restarting (cold start downloads rasters) when the page loads.
break_it.what_happens: Gates proxy returns 502, hook gives null, page shows 'Not checked' for the area.
break_it.how: Proxy 502 -> null gates; no default to true.

break_it.scenario: The TypeScript eligibility route and the Python engine still differ on other standards.
break_it.what_happens: Height/FSR override display and other form logic remain two implementations that could disagree.
break_it.how: Out of scope; flagged follow-up to consolidate the route into the Python engine (DQ-30).

post_merge.manual_verify: Yes - after Railway and Vercel deploy: GET /pipeline/housing-sepp/gates for Winston Hills returns in_lmr_area false; the assessment page for 6 Berrigan St Winston Hills shows 'Not in a Low and Mid-Rise housing area' and multi-dwelling not eligible.

residual_risk: Two eligibility implementations remain (DQ-30). A map outage shows 'Not checked' rather than an answer.
